decision.summary: Harbour Services is booked to inspect the oven on 22 May at 2:30pm, and has said the oven is out of warranty. I told the landlord, tenant and contractor. No chargeable work will go ahead without landlord approval of a quote. No human decision is needed yet.

answers.question: Where does this case stand right now, and what is outstanding?
answers.answer: Landlord approval to proceed was confirmed and Harbour Services is assigned. The visit is agreed with the tenant for 22 May at 2:30pm. Harbour says the oven is out of warranty, so the landlord's request for a free warranty repair no longer applies. Outstanding: the inspection, a quote if needed, landlord approval of any cost, and clarification of the install date and installer.

answers.question: What is the next action, who is it for, and through which channel?
answers.answer: Emails sent to the landlord (warranty outcome, quote-approval process, installer query), the tenant (visit confirmation) and the contractor (confirm the date, send a quote and do not proceed without approval, confirm the install date). Next, wait for the inspection and any quote.

answers.question: Does anything need a human decision, and why?
answers.answer: Not at this point. If the quote is above the landlord's limit, or the landlord disputes the warranty position, the quote needs landlord approval. A human is only needed if the landlord does not reply or the install-date conflict affects a warranty claim.

actions_claimed.description: Emailed landlord with warranty outcome and approval process
Emailed tenant confirming the visit on 22 May at 2:30pm
Emailed contractor to confirm the date, ask for a quote before work and confirm the install date

conflicts: Event 014 says the oven was replaced in March 2025, which is in the future. The tenant says last year. Asked the contractor to confirm.
Contractor emails say the visit is 'tomorrow, 21st June', but today is 21 May. The call record says the next day at 2:30pm, so I treated it as 22 May.
The landlord named Keystone Works as the installer, but the notes say Harbour Services. Asked the landlord to confirm.
The ticket list tool returned no tickets, although the case history shows an open request.
assumptions: The visit is on 22 May at 2:30pm, per the call record.
The oven is out of warranty, per the contractor's statement only, with no document seen.

They are visiting the tenant tomorrow (22 May) at 2:30pm to inspect. If a quote is needed, we will send it to you and will not go ahead with any chargeable work until you approve it. Please also let us know your spend limit for this repair if you have one. One thing to check: your note mentioned Keystone Works fitting the oven, but our records show Harbour Services did. Please let us know which is right, in case there is a warranty claim with another company. Kind regards
